title: Minimax Estimation of Normalized Extreme Treatment Effects under a Shrinking Moment Gap
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 graded the sound exact-Pareto matched frontier incremental below the field floor and not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The note proves the advertised matched rate and consistency criterion, but only in a highly structured scalar exact-Pareto product experiment where threshold invariance follows mechanically from exponential memorylessness and amplitude–excess independence.
Consequently, the result is a worthwhile specialized boundary analysis rather than a field-level causal-extremes theorem that practitioners could use under standard tail modeling.
The projected paper score is constrained by this narrow exact-model scope and by the absence of a theorem-level robustness result connecting the frontier to realistic extreme-value experiments.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the exact threshold-invariant NETE embedding, a protected estimator upper bound, and matching fixed-alpha Pareto-KL and unknown-alpha Hellinger lower paths, yielding the advertised capped minimax and absolute-consistency frontiers. The mathematics passed review, but the field-tier program collapsed on scope: extending it to second-order tails would replace the identification, estimator, bias, and converse kernels rather than repair this specialization. A future re-raised run should reuse the exact-model core as a benchmark while building that new robustness theory.
tldr: The note proves the sharp uniform absolute-RMSE frontier for the Tan--Blanchet--Syrgkanis normalized extreme treatment effect in an unknown-growth, exact scalar-Pareto product subclass.  For every deterministic \(t\ge u\), the normalized causal effect is exactly threshold invariant: \(t^{-\alpha}\mathbb E[Y_1-Y_0\mid R>t]=\eta\beta/(\beta-\alpha)\).  Hence the finite-threshold target is literally the asymptotic NETE.  From the induced randomized observed experiment, its matched capped frontier is \(\min\{d^{-1},(\sqrt{k}d^2)^{-1}+(1+\log u)/(\sqrt{k}d)\}\), with the corresponding two-condition absolute-consistency boundary.  The result is for this strict exact-Pareto subclass; adaptive efficiency, random thresholds, second-order tails, and applied consumers remain outside the kernel.
gap: NETE is identified as a treatment contrast times a Pareto radial moment, and existing analyses expose logarithmic sensitivity to estimating outcome growth. What remains unresolved is the uniform observed-data decision problem over explicitly specified full-data laws as the moment gap approaches zero: the inspected causal-tail, expected-shortfall, and tail-index literature does not give both lower paths, all saturation regimes, and the absolute-risk cap.
fill: Prove observed-data identification and full-data extension invariance, a protected estimator with unconditional random-count risk, and exact full-data alternatives whose induced observed marginals obey common-constant KL/Hellinger bounds; then assemble the regimes into a matched minimax and probability-form consistency frontier.
